newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton weak on sluggish demand, monsoon fear.
newsitem.headline: India cotton weak on sluggish demand, monsoon fear.

text.p: Cotton prices turned weak on the local market on Wednesday, dealers said.
Mill demand was sluggish while the progress of the monsoon in producing centres prompted unloading by stockists.
"Last week market was firm on dry spell but fresh rain in producing centres has cooled down the prices," one trader said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 10 rupees at 1,000/1,075 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned slid by 5/10 rupees at 1,820/1,850 rupees per maund.

In the Gujarat segment, Kalyan cotton fell by 100 rupees at 14,100/14,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Wagad cotton dropped by 100 rupees at 13,000/13,100 rupees and Kala-ginned by 100 rupees at 12,300/12,400 rupees per candy.
Most millers have enough cotton stocks to last them 2/3 months and demand from them remained low in the ready delivery.
